articleBody:
Before groundbreaking starts on an expanded kitchen footprint, having your site conditions, permits, and plans verified prevents expensive construction delays. Use this practical preparation list before work begins.

- [ ] Property boundary survey — verifies setback distances and prevents building over property lines.
- [ ] Municipal permit approval — confirms structural, zoning, and fire review clearances before demolition.
- [ ] Structural plan review — ensures the connection between the existing foundation, framing, and new roof is engineered properly.
- [ ] Utility capacity assessment — checks whether extending plumbing, gas, and electrical circuits requires panel or line upgrades.
- [ ] Site drainage check — guarantees the ground slopes away from the new foundation walls to prevent moisture issues.
- [ ] Written change-order terms — defines how unexpected structural or site discoveries are priced and approved.
- [ ] Material allowance schedule — locks in specific budgets for cabinetry, flooring, windows, and countertops.
- [ ] Trade coordination schedule — outlines who manages framing, plumbing rough-ins, drywall, and finish carpentry.

How to use this checklist

Review these items directly with your builder before signing a contract or ordering materials. Starting site work without approved plans or underestimating utility extensions often leads to work stoppages. Having these concrete details documented ensures smooth inspections and realistic milestones.
